Overall great game! Reminds me of Uplink.

+ Pros

*Fast-paced at times
*Makes you think
*Not overly complicated (you do not have to be a programmer to understand it, basic computer knowledge will do fine)
*Proper community  - developers are very hands-on for this project, they have made everything understandable and information can easily be found online from different aspects. Also, players are giving hints online about things and avoid telling you too much ahead, keeps the fun in the game. I like that approach.
*Workshop system - developers seemed to have made it simple for everyone to make their own story in this game.

Cons

*Longetivity. I've finished main game in 4 hours. Tried an popular extension (which one, does not really matter), but in reality, it's the same thing from a different angle.
*Deepness. Besides from objectives, I would've liked a little bit of upgrade/economy system, which it does not have.

Would I recommend it? Ofcourse. It's been very cheap since it came out with loads of promotions along the way. It's not something to keep you occupied for weeks, but as a throwback to Uplink scene or as a couple-hour-play from time to time, it will be perfect.

This is one of those games that makes you wish for a 'meh' rating. I'm three hours in and the narrative isn't really picking up. The soundtrack is excellent, the use of real console commands is cool, and hacking feels pretty fun -- it scratches that fantasy of being a shady, smart hacker... but provides none of the challenge. The hacking is easy and the contracts largely repetitive outside of a few good gags. There's no real moral choices and ultimately, the game just doesn't hook you in as much after a while. A stronger narrative, more choices and better puzzles would serve this game well. The best moment I experienced came when I was counter-hacked, and had to reboot my system by navigating only with the terminal. But the moment-to-moment gameplay requires no such thought.

Still, a lot of people seem to enjoy that core fantasy and find the narrative engaging enough to keep going, and if you're really into the game, the mod support is excellent. 

Tl;dr it's fine, if you enjoy the core fantasy a lot there's a lot of good stuff there for you, but otherwise it's let down by disappointing gameplay.
